content.value_statement: UI work can drift into hard-coded spacing, colors, and raw platform components. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code toward core components, tokens, and reusable layouts.
actual_capabilities: Explains spacing, color, and typography token usage.
Shows core components such as Box, Text, Button, Input, and Card.
Provides HStack and VStack layout patterns.
Gives screen, form, and list item layout examples.
Lists UI anti-patterns and token-based alternatives.
Describes component prop patterns for reusable components.
limitations: It is documentation only and does not include executable component source.
Token names and components must match the user project.
It does not validate rendered UI or run tests.
It does not cover accessibility rules beyond component usage.

use_cases.title: Standardize New Screens
use_cases.description: Build screens with Screen, ScreenHeader, ScreenContent, and token spacing from the start.

use_cases.title: Refactor Raw UI
use_cases.description: Replace raw platform components and inline styles with core components and design tokens.

use_cases.title: Review Component APIs
use_cases.description: Design reusable component props that expose tokens, variants, and children consistently.

prompt_templates.title: Use Core Components
prompt_templates.prompt: Build this screen using the core component library. Use token spacing, semantic colors, and no raw platform components: [screen details].

prompt_templates.title: Apply Design Tokens
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this UI description and choose spacing, color, and typography tokens. Explain each token choice briefly: [UI details].

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Existing Markup
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this component to use Box, Text, HStack, VStack, Button, Input, and Card where appropriate. Preserve behavior and remove inline styles: [component].

prompt_templates.title: Design Reusable Component API
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a reusable component API using token-based props, variants, loading and disabled states, and clear composition boundaries: [requirements].

output_examples.input: Create a settings screen with profile details and a save action.
output_examples.output: The response recommends Screen, ScreenHeader, ScreenContent, VStack, Input, and Button with token spacing and semantic colors.

output_examples.input: Review a form that uses raw platform components and inline styles.
output_examples.output: The response identifies each raw component, maps it to the core library, and replaces hard-coded values with tokens.

output_examples.input: Plan a reusable card component for several product states.
output_examples.output: The response defines token-based props, variants, children composition, and state handling for loading and disabled views.

best_practices: Use design tokens for spacing, color, and typography.
Prefer core layout components before raw platform primitives.
Keep reusable component props token-based and variant-driven.
anti_patterns: Hard-coding pixel spacing, hex colors, or typography values.
Mixing raw platform components into screens that should use the core library.
Adding inline styles where token props would be clearer.

faq.question: Does this skill install a component library?
faq.answer: No. It gives usage guidance for an existing core component library.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. It is written as guidance that these AI coding tools can follow.

faq.question: Does it support React Native?
faq.answer: The examples use React Native-style patterns and work best when similar components exist.

faq.question: Will it choose exact project tokens?
faq.answer: It recommends token categories, but you should verify names against your project theme.

faq.question: Does it replace accessibility review?
faq.answer: No. You still need accessibility checks, platform testing, and design review.

faq.question: When should I avoid using it?
faq.answer: Avoid it when the project lacks a core component library or approved design tokens.
